basics.name: Adrian Góra
basics.label: AI / Software Engineer | LLM apps, RAG, agents | TypeScript, Python
basics.summary: AI Engineer at Wiśniowski since February 2025, building internal tools for document search, translation, meeting reports and production analysis. Before that, four years of TypeScript and React in fintech and Web3.

work.name: Wiśniowski
work.summary: Internal AI tools for a Polish manufacturer of industrial doors, gates and fences.
highlights: Deployed RAGFlow on a Linux server and connected it to Open WebUI as the company chat. It answers from the company's technical PDFs with complex layouts. Telemetry and monitoring are built for EU AI Act compliance.

Scans one group's meetings in on-premises Outlook and switches on automatic recording. Transcripts and recordings come in through Microsoft Graph (webhooks and polling), and an LLM turns them into structured JSON reports.

Built an internal portal to replace lokalise.com. Gemini pre-translates every key, translators accept or fix it, and missing keys are flagged. To keep terms consistent across languages, I added statistics, translator helpers and a generated starting glossary. Every decision is logged, which shows how often the AI is right.

Working on a prototype that lets engineers chat with historical production traces, test new settings and get suggested routes. A deterministic core computes the numbers, and experimental modules add an LLM and autoresearch.

After a 15-minute voice or text interview about someone's daily work, it writes an automation report, adds what it learned to an LLM wiki and turns repeatable tasks into SKILL.md files for agents. Runs on the Gemini managed-agents sandbox.

projects.name: PDF-Insight: validated document extraction
projects.description: Inspects PDFs locally, redacts sensitive text and extracts summaries, parties, amounts and dates as validated JSON. Shared Zod schemas connect the React frontend, Cloudflare Worker and Gemini responses.
highlights: Original PDF bytes remain local; only redacted text reaches the API.
Checks amounts and dates against source text and flags values it cannot verify. These checks do not establish the accuracy of every summary sentence.
Benchmark: 19 of 20 public uploads completed within 30 seconds; maximum 41.0 seconds. Long-term reliability remains under observation.

projects.name: Cairn: process-route analysis
projects.description: Shows where work waits, where it loops back and which routing choice succeeded more often once the mix of work is held fixed. Every number opens into the records behind it. The code is private; the live demo runs on public datasets, and its free hosting can take a minute to wake up.
highlights: Each claim carries its sample size, basis and whether it may be quoted, and a marked finding can be re-proved on new data.
The CLI prints one JSON envelope per call, with ready-to-quote sentences, caveats and refused questions, so an AI agent can use it without inventing numbers.
The demo opens on online retail orders (UCI, CC BY 4.0); the factory data the tool was built for stays private. Includes a robot-fleet dispatch testbed (VDA 5050).

projects.name: VisualRAG
projects.description: Searches technical PDFs using page images and BM25 text retrieval, then answers with citations to source pages.
highlights: Hybrid retrieval fuses page-image matches with BM25 text matches using Reciprocal Rank Fusion.
Seven retrieval modes can be compared in the web UI; answers cite the retrieved source pages.

projects.name: CAD quoting engine for machined parts
projects.description: Quotes a machined part from its STEP file (a 3D CAD model) for a tool shop. Code measures the part and computes the price; an AI model reviews the machining process and risks the way a shop manager would.
highlights: Volume, mass, envelope and cost-driving features come from OpenCASCADE. Price is machining time × shop rate, and a physics-based floor on cutting time stops the model from inventing hours.
Preflight marks each check pass, fail or need-info with a cited source (ISO 2768, ISO 286, material data). Any fail or missing input makes the quote non-binding.
Web app for estimators who don't program: 3D preview, 2D drawing input, editable rates, print to PDF and a make-or-buy check against SendCutSend. Covered by 8 test modules.

projects.name: LLM-judged translation audit
projects.description: Finds inconsistent terms in translations that never had a glossary. Code finds the disagreements across 7,040 texts, and an AI model decides each one.
highlights: Exports an Excel workbook for sign-off and a keyboard-driven review app where translators curate the glossary; decided terms are never re-arbitrated.
Sibling demo judge-sheets: type a column header such as Urgency and 300 rows fill with semantic predictions in about 3.5 s, as =JUDGE, =PICK and =RATE formulas you can inspect in the formula bar.
